about: Catalog of things a user can have in a chat and would expect in an export. Driven by tools/live.js (prepare/collect) and tests/live/TASK.md (Claude Desktop). support: what the extension is expected to handle today -- 'supported' failures are reported as BROKEN, 'unsupported'/'unknown' failures as GAPS, and an unsupported feature that passes as NEWLY WORKING. cost 'high' features (quota-hungry) run only with --include-expensive. automation 'manual' features are listed but never automated. context: new test chats start in the provider test project when config.local.json lists the provider in useProjectFor; outside-project / project force one or the other.

features.title: Thinking (claude.ai keeps only summaries)

features.title: Web search with cited sources
features.prompt: Search the web: what is the latest stable version of Node.js? Cite your source.
features.notes: Checks that a source link survives in the answer. When text blocks carry citations[] the export adds [[n]](url) markers and a Sources list (covered by claude.mixed / claude.research); when Claude writes the sources itself (citations: [] -- the 2026-10-01 chat) they are plain markdown links. Don't toggle tools in the composer -- if web search is off, the answer has no sources and that's fine to report.

features.title: Everything at once: images + PDF + text file, thinking, web search, artifact created then updated, generated file, tricky formatting
features.setup: Turn on extended thinking and web search in the composer.
features.prompt: Mixed export test. Using all attached files: describe both images in one line each, give the project codename from the PDF, and list the action items from the notes. Also search the web for the current version of Node.js. In your answer include one sentence in Ukrainian, an emoji, the formula $E=mc^2$, and a markdown code block whose content contains a line with three backticks.
followUps: Send: Now create an artifact: a markdown report that combines all of the above, with a table.
Send: Update that artifact: add a section called Next steps with 3 bullets.
Send: Use code execution to create summary.json with the codename and budget, and give it to me as a downloadable file.
features.notes: Catches interactions: uploads next to artifacts, artifact versions, thinking interleaved with tool use, nested code fences, non-Latin text.
